data.title: Pearly penile papules — viva
data.summary: Benign tumours & cysts · 15 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Pearly penile papules** (Benign tumours & cysts)_

**Q1. What are pearly penile papules (PPP)?**
- Common normal anatomical variant (angiofibromas — hirsuties coronae glandis) in 15–45% of men (more in uncircumcised, young adults): small (1–3 mm), smooth, dome-shaped or filiform, pearly white to skin-coloured papules arranged in one or several symmetrical rows around the corona and sulcus of the glans; asymptomatic, not infectious, not sexually transmitted

**Q2. Histopathology.**
- Angiofibroma: dense fibrous stroma with stellate fibroblasts and dilated thin-walled vessels covered by normal or slightly thinned epidermis (same as facial angiofibroma)

**Q3. Discuss non-venereal genital lesions (PYQ).**
- Normal variants: PPP, Fordyce spots (ectopic sebaceous glands — yellow papules on shaft/labia), vestibular papillae (women — symmetrical filiform papules of vestibule; female counterpart of PPP), Tyson's glands, median raphe cysts, angiokeratomas of scrotum (Fordyce)
- Dermatoses: psoriasis, lichen planus (annular on glans), lichen sclerosus (BXO), lichen nitidus, seborrhoeic dermatitis, Zoon's balanitis (plasma cell balanitis — glistening red-orange plaque on glans of uncircumcised elderly), fixed drug eruption, contact dermatitis, candidal balanoposthitis, scabies nodules, vitiligo
- Neoplastic: erythroplasia of Queyrat, bowenoid papulosis, SCC, extramammary Paget's, Kaposi sarcoma

**Q4. Differential diagnosis.**
- Genital warts (condyloma acuminata — irregular, random distribution, cauliflower surface, acetowhite), molluscum contagiosum (umbilicated, scattered), Fordyce spots (shaft, yellow), sebaceous hyperplasia, lichen nitidus, ectopic sebaceous glands, angiokeratomas

**Q5. Why does it matter in clinics?**
- Commonly mistaken for genital warts by patients and doctors → anxiety ('venereophobia'), unnecessary destructive treatment; dermoscopy shows uniform papules with central comma/dotted vessels without the mosaic pattern of warts

**Q6. Management.**
- Reassurance and education (no treatment needed)
- For cosmetic/psychological distress: CO2 laser vaporisation, fractional CO2, pulsed-dye laser, radiofrequency, cryotherapy (variable) — warn about scarring and recurrence

**Q7. Discuss non-venereal genital dermatoses (expanded list).**
- Normal variants: PPP, Fordyce spots, Tyson's glands, median raphe cysts
- Inflammatory: psoriasis, LP, LS (BXO), seborrhoeic/ contact dermatitis, Zoon's balanitis, FDE, aphthae/ Behçet's, candidal/ irritant balanoposthitis
- Infections (non-STI): tinea cruris, scabies nodules, erythrasma
- Neoplastic/ premalignant: erythroplasia of Queyrat, bowenoid papulosis, SCC, extramammary Paget's, angiokeratomas of Fordyce (scrotum), sebaceous/ epidermoid cysts, lymphangioma

**Q8. What are angiokeratomas of Fordyce?**
- Multiple small dark-red/ purple papules on scrotum/ vulva of older adults — dilated superficial vessels with hyperkeratosis; benign; differentiate from angiokeratoma corporis diffusum (Fabry disease — 'bathing trunk' distribution, pain crises, renal failure)

**Q9. Treatment options when requested.**
- Reassurance is best; for persistent anxiety — CO2 laser ablation, cryotherapy, radiofrequency; avoid podophyllin/ imiquimod (ineffective, irritating)

**Q10. Psychosexual aspects — venereophobia.**
- Anxiety that normal genital variants are STIs; counsel, examine and test as needed, explain benign nature, consider psychiatric referral for persistent illness anxiety (venereophobia, Dhat syndrome in Indian context)

**Q11. What is Zoon's balanitis?**
- Plasma cell balanitis — well-defined, glistening orange-red plaque with 'cayenne pepper' spots on glans/ inner prepuce of uncircumcised older men; histology — dense plasma cell infiltrate; differentiate from erythroplasia of Queyrat (biopsy); circumcision curative

**Q12. Dhat syndrome — what is it?**
- Culture-bound syndrome in South Asia: young men attribute fatigue, anxiety, sexual weakness to loss of semen in urine/ nocturnal emissions; associated depression/ anxiety; manage with explanation, sex education, treat underlying psychiatric disorder

**Q13. What is the prevalence and natural history?**
- Present in ~15–45% of men (more in uncircumcised, young adults); appear after puberty, may fade with age; not sexually transmitted, not related to hygiene, benign and permanent

**Q14. Dermoscopy of PPP vs genital warts.**
- PPP: regular 'cobblestone' or grape-like arrangement of uniform papules with central dotted/comma vessels in rows along the corona
- Warts: irregular papillomatous lesions with glomerular/ hairpin vessels and white network, mosaic pattern

**Q15. Female counterpart?**
- Vestibular papillomatosis — symmetrical, soft, separate-based papillae on the inner labia minora/vestibule; normal variant (may be confused with warts — acetowhite test can falsely be positive)

## Quick spotter facts
- Symmetrical rows of pearly dome papules around the corona — PPP (normal variant, angiofibroma)
- Do not treat as warts

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Normal variants of genitalia; non-venereal genital lesions). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
